clue.text: Drinks up when aboard ship

indicators.note: to be aboard is to be on a ship, so one piece sits between the two letters of the other

parts.note: SS is the standard abbreviation for steamship

explanation.surface: Someone finishes their drinks once they are on board a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when' is only a link; the definition is the verb 'Drinks'.
explanation.definitionFit: To sup is to take liquid in sips or mouthfuls, a slightly old-fashioned synonym for drinking.

clue.text: Cobra and tulips out of place in a fairly lush climate

indicators.note: letters that are out of place have been moved from their proper positions, so the two words are jumbled

explanation.surface: A snake and some flowers look wrong in a warm, lush part of the world.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of place' signals rearranging all the letters of COBRA and TULIPS together.
explanation.definitionFit: Regions bordering the tropics have warm, fairly humid weather and rich vegetation, just short of tropical.

clue.text: Working to initiate start of play in Test

indicators.note: one piece is placed in the middle of the other, as the clue's preposition says

parts.note: to prove something is to test it, as in proving a theory or a gun
the opening of a play is Act One, written ACT I

explanation.surface: Reads like a cricket report: someone busy getting the first ball of a Test match bowled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'start of play' looks like a first-letter instruction, but it means ACT I, the first act of a drama. 'Test' is a verb here, not the cricket match.
explanation.definitionFit: A proactive person takes the initiative, acting in advance to make things happen rather than reacting.

clue.text: American guy to board silent plane? Nonsense

indicators.note: boarding means getting on, so the guy goes into the middle of the other two pieces

parts.note: to keep mum is to stay silent
a jumbo is a jumbo jet, a large aircraft
BO is American slang for a fellow or pal

explanation.surface: An American man getting on a quiet jet, then the whole thing dismissed as nonsense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'American guy' is US slang for a pal; the '?' marks the jet as a plane only loosely.
explanation.definitionFit: Meaningless or deliberately obscure talk or ritual is commonly called by this reduplicated phrase.

clue.text: Meal without starter has reduced punch

indicators.note: a meal without its starter loses its first course, here its first letter

parts.note: supper is an evening meal
a cut price is a reduced one

explanation.surface: A dinner served with no first course has a weaker punch to it, like a watered-down drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without starter' takes the first letter S off SUPPER, leaving UPPER.
explanation.definitionFit: A boxing blow thrown upward from below, usually aimed at the opponent's chin.

clue.text: Less tactful, outing 'large' schoolboy

indicators.note: outing here means putting out, so the letter is expelled from the word

parts.note: blunter means more outspoken, less tactful
L is the standard abbreviation for large, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: A tactless remark exposes a fat schoolboy, with 'large' in mock quotes as a polite word.
explanation.walkthrough: Billy Bunter is the greedy, fat pupil of Greyfriars School in Frank Richards's stories, a famous figure in British comics; the 'large' quote marks hint at him.
explanation.definitionFit: The best-known fictional pupil of that name is Billy, the fat boy of Greyfriars School.

clue.text: Project on English fibre

parts.note: to project is to stick out, or jut

explanation.surface: A project about English fibre, like a school assignment on textiles.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' means the second piece sits below the first.
explanation.definitionFit: A coarse plant fibre from South Asia used for sacking, hessian and rope.

clue.text: Spots second article from Libération

parts.note: a mo is a moment, a second
les is a French plural definite article, apt for the French paper Libération

explanation.surface: Someone spots a second piece in the French newspaper Libération.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spots' looks like a verb but is the plural noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Moles are small dark marks on the skin, a kind of spot or blemish.

clue.text: Eggs on very assiduously at the start

indicators.note: the starts of these three words are taken, one letter from each

explanation.surface: Someone urges another on very diligently from the beginning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eggs on' reads as a phrasal verb, but 'Eggs' alone is the definition and 'on' gives a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Ova is the Latin plural for egg cells, used in biology for female reproductive cells.

clue.text: Former PM to respond to Sun?

definitions.meaning: Gordon, the UK prime minister who followed Tony Blair in 2007
skin responds to sunshine by tanning, darkening in colour

explanation.surface: A former prime minister responding to the Sun newspaper, a British tabloid.
explanation.walkthrough: The Sun is a British tabloid, and the surface suggests a politician answering it; the capital S hides the plain meaning of sunshine.
explanation.definitionFit: The surname of a recent UK prime minister is also a verb for going tan in sunlight.

clue.text: Arm raised — under it a right-winger of little merit

indicators.note: in a down clue what comes under a piece follows it
in a down clue raised means written upwards, so the word is read in reverse

parts.note: a gun is a firearm, a weapon or arm
a Tory is a member of Britain's Conservative Party

explanation.surface: A weapon held up, and beneath it a worthless right-wing politician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns GUN into NUG.
explanation.definitionFit: A rather formal word meaning futile, trifling or worthless, of no real value or effect.

clue.text: Article wedged in part of skeleton is a cigar

indicators.note: something wedged in is forced inside, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: the patella is the kneecap bone
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Odd anatomy: a newspaper article stuck in a bone turns out to be a cigar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A long, slender cigar, the name also spelt with one L.

clue.text: Display of plants implying danger?

parts.note: a bed of alpine plants set among stones; stones in the sea are a hazard to shipping, hence the hint of danger

explanation.surface: A flower show that somehow looks threatening.
explanation.walkthrough: A ship heading for the rocks is in danger, so the stony half of the planting suggests peril.
explanation.definitionFit: A garden area built of stones and boulders for alpine and other small plants.

clue.text: Continent, one occupying a small area

indicators.note: to occupy a place is to be inside it, so one piece goes within the others

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A continent where one person takes up only a tiny space.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a small area' supplies three letters, A, S and A.
explanation.definitionFit: The largest of the world's landmasses, stretching from the Urals to the Pacific.

clue.text: Great manner may be seen in this of itself

definitions.text: Great manner may be seen in this of itself

indicators.text: may be seen in this of itself
indicators.note: the clue says the answer itself is the reordering, so the two words are to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A grand style is evident in the thing itself.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is its own anagram signal: a reordering of GREAT MANNER, and a word for an ordering, so the whole clue is both definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A rearrangement or ordering of things, which is just what the two clue words undergo.

clue.text: Something stirring about poster for driver or pedestrian

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece goes round the other

parts.note: a rouser is something that rouses or stirs people up
an ad is an advertisement, such as a poster

explanation.surface: A provocative billboard aimed at motorists and walkers, like a road-safety campaign.
explanation.walkthrough: 'poster' is an advertisement, not someone who posts.
explanation.definitionFit: Anyone travelling on a highway, whether on foot or at the wheel, falls under this term.

clue.text: All in French, following principal material from computer

indicators.note: following means coming after, so the French word goes second

parts.note: Prin. is a dictionary abbreviation for principal
tout is French for all

explanation.surface: Everything in a French lesson, prepared after the head teacher, printed off a computer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'principal' gives an abbreviation, not a synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: Paper output produced by a computer's printer is known by this term.

clue.text: Conspirator without latitude to move unhurriedly

indicators.note: without means lacking, so the letter is removed

parts.note: a plotter is one who conspires
L is the abbreviation for latitude on maps

explanation.surface: A schemer, given no leeway, is reduced to wandering about slowly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'latitude' looks like freedom in the surface but is the map abbreviation L.
explanation.definitionFit: To dawdle or amble about aimlessly, pottering in the garden being the British image.

clue.text: Reprimand tense singer after embracing monarch

parts.note: T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense

indicators.note: to embrace is to hug, so one piece wraps around the other

parts.note: an alto is a singer with a low female or high male voice
a king is a male monarch

explanation.surface: A nervous vocalist is told off after hugging the king.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tense' is a grammar abbreviation, not nervousness; ALTO holds KING after its first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A scolding or telling-off given to someone who has misbehaved, used as a noun.

clue.text: A lot of discussion, not entirely pleasant, regarding Jewish teaching

indicators.note: a lot of something is most but not all of it, so the last letter goes

parts.note: rabbit is British slang for chatter, from rhyming slang rabbit and pork for talk

indicators.note: not entirely means incompletely, so the word loses its final letter

parts.note: nice means pleasant

explanation.surface: A long, somewhat unpleasant discussion about Jewish doctrine.
explanation.walkthrough: RABBIT (talk, from British rhyming slang) loses its last letter, and NICE loses its E.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to rabbis, the Jewish scholars and teachers, or to their writings and law.

clue.text: Fruit to be sinful? Church variable about that

indicators.note: about means around, and that points back to the sinning word, which the others go round

parts.note: Y is a standard algebraic variable
to err is to sin or go wrong

explanation.surface: Echoes the forbidden fruit: is eating it a sin, and is the Church's view changeable?
explanation.walkthrough: 'that' points back to 'to be sinful', the piece the other two wrap around.
explanation.definitionFit: A small round stone fruit, usually red, from trees of the genus Prunus.

clue.text: New and old mingling in important stringed instrument

indicators.note: in signals one piece placed inside another

parts.note: main means chief or important

indicators.note: things mingling are mixed together, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Old and new styles blend in a significant string instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and' is only a link; 'mingling' scrambles just the new-and-old letters into NDOL, and 'in' sets that inside the word for important.
explanation.definitionFit: A lute-like instrument with paired metal strings, played with a plectrum.

clue.text: Satisfied rising building will conceal current religious building

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means written upwards, so the word reads backwards

parts.note: a need that is met is satisfied

indicators.note: to conceal is to hide away, so the letter disappears from the word

parts.note: a pile is a large building
I is the physics symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: A content new building going up will hide an electrical current inside a place of worship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' turns MET into TEM; PILE loses I to give PLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A building devoted to worship, especially in Judaism, Hinduism or ancient religions.

clue.text: US city to succeed in disposing of one grassy area

parts.note: LA is Los Angeles

indicators.note: disposing of something gets rid of it, so the letter is dropped

parts.note: to win is to succeed
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A Los Angeles bid to win by getting rid of somebody over a patch of grass.
explanation.walkthrough: WIN loses I to leave WN.
explanation.definitionFit: A stretch of mown grass in a garden or park.

clue.text: Elevated argument over this is lacking value

indicators.note: in a down clue over means placed above, so this piece comes first
in a down clue elevated means lifted up, so the word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: a row is a quarrel or argument

indicators.note: lacking means without, so the two letters are removed from the word

explanation.surface: A heated argument over this being of no value.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Elevated' turns ROW into WOR; THIS lacking IS leaves TH.
explanation.definitionFit: The value or merit of something, as in its worth to a buyer.

clue.text: Flurry of birds here around Wye? This is somewhere else

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so the jumble goes round the single letter
a flurry is a confused bustle, so these letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: Wye is the spoken name of the letter Y, and also a river

explanation.surface: A flurry of birds round the River Wye, an English-Welsh river; this is another place altogether.
explanation.walkthrough: Derbyshire is an English county. 'somewhere else' is witty because the fodder held 'here'; the jumble DERBSHIRE goes round the letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An English county in the East Midlands, a place other than 'here' since that word was scrambled away.

clue.text: Much-loved daughter is getting attention

parts.note: to give someone your ear is to give them attention

explanation.surface: A beloved daughter is the centre of attention.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is getting' is a link joining the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A word for someone cherished or held in great affection.

clue.text: Writer to observe Queen encountering swan

parts.note: to mark is to notice or observe
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen
a pen is a female swan

explanation.surface: An author watches the Queen meet a swan, the birds traditionally owned by the British monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'encountering' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A felt-tipped writing tool with thick ink, a writer in the sense of an implement.

clue.text: Extinct bird located in Palermo, actually

indicators.note: located in signals letters found within the run of clue words

explanation.surface: An extinct bird was in fact found in the Sicilian city of Palermo.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters straddle the end of 'Palermo' and the start of 'actually'.
explanation.definitionFit: A huge flightless bird of New Zealand, hunted to extinction several centuries ago.

clue.text: Unreliable parachute dismissed at outset

indicators.note: something dismissed at the outset is lost from the very beginning, so the first letter goes

parts.note: a drogue is a small parachute used to slow or stabilise an aircraft or capsule

explanation.surface: A faulty parachute rejected before a jump even begins.
explanation.walkthrough: DROGUE loses its first letter D.
explanation.definitionFit: Used adjectivally for something errant or unpredictable, as a rogue element or rogue trader.

clue.text: Hate misuse of carbon here

indicators.note: misusing letters puts them to wrong use, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: An environmentalist's loathing for the misuse of carbon in this place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'misuse of' jumbles the letters of CARBON and HERE together.
explanation.definitionFit: A feeling of intense loathing or disgust, a strong synonym for hatred.

clue.text: The same officer is a fool

parts.note: do is short for ditto, meaning the same
Lt is the abbreviation for lieutenant, an officer

explanation.surface: The same officer, again, is an idiot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A stupid person, a dunce or blockhead.
